/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 19 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3054 (-38)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4949 (-64)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2459 (-52)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1568 (-2)
Baltic Handysize Index: 850 (-2)
CAPESIZE
A slightly mixed day for the Capesize market, with improving sentiment and healthier activity levels in the Pacific helping rates edge higher, while the Atlantic basin softened marginally amid quieter conditions. The BCI 182 5TC slipped by $574 to close at $44,888. In the Pacific, conditions appeared more positive as operator-controlled cargoes increased, while all three major miners were notably more active on C5. Early indications saw offers begin around the $15 level with bids reported in the low $14s, though momentum gradually improved as the day progressed. Fixtures initially surfaced around the $14.65-$14.70 range before later business was concluded at $14.80 and eventually $14.95, reflecting the stronger undertone. Consequently, C5 managed to nudge up by 0.150 to $14.940. Overall sentiment in the basin improved as volumes looked healthier than in recent sessions. Conversely, the Atlantic basin experienced a quieter and slightly softer trading environment. Activity on C3 remained relatively subdued, with minimal spreads discussed around index dates. For the 20/26 June window, reports circulated of $36.50 being paid, while market talk suggested bids remained closer to $36.75. Despite this, C3 slipped marginally by $0.155 to settle at $36.450.
PANAMAX
The Panamax market posted another day of index losses, with the P5TC average falling by $466 to close at $22,131. In the Atlantic, front-haul activity remained muted while the East Coast South America market continued to weaken. In Asia, cargo availability in the North Pacific remains limited compared with the still-lengthy tonnage list in the region. Continued pressure from East Australia and Indonesia cargo flows is also keeping owners on the defensive. With spot tonnage supply continuing to outpace demand, some market participants believe further downward pressure is likely.

Atlantic
While some sources described the rate as very strong, the Meltemi (82,206 2022) was heard fixed for a trip from EC South America with delivery 9/12 June and redelivery at Djen Djen carrying minerals at $43,500, reportedly to Oldendorff further details could not be confirmed. Meanwhile, the Africa Graeca II (82,712 2026) was heard fixed delivery retro Trincomalee 16 May via EC South America to the Singapore/Japan with grains at $27,000, although some sources suggested the rate was lower and that this was an older fixture.

Asia
The Moana Infinity (88,233 2002) open Singapore 20/22 May was placed on subjects for an Indonesia round voyage, although no further details were reported. The Star Electra (83,494 2011), scrubber-fitted and open Kimitsu on 22 May was also placed on subjects for a North Pacific round voyage, again with no additional details available. In addition, the Flag Tom (93,268 2011), open Taichung 25/26 May, was placed on subjects, with no further details disclosed.
SUPRAMAX
A slight change in tempo for the sector today which was described as positional. The Atlantic was a mixed affair, brokers saying that whilst demand remains from the US Gulf there appeared to be a widening gap between owners and charterers expectations. The South Atlantic was finely balanced although some felt a ceiling may have been reached as demand eased on the larger Kamsamax size. It became apparent during the course of the day, that the Asian arena was starting the week at a slow pace. Prompt tonnage availability from the south combined with slow fresh enquiry further north saw downward pressure appear across most areas. The 11TC average closed down $27 at $19,822.

Atlantic
It was reported that DK Ione (58,714 2010) was fixed for a scrap run basis delivery Continent prompt trip to the East Mediterranean at $18,000. Otherwise, little fresh information surfaced.

Asia
The Xin Ming Zhou 27 (57,450 2012) was heard fixed basis delivery Singapore for a trip via Indonesia redelivery China at $18,000, but no more details came to light.

HANDYSIZE
The Handy market delivered another mixed performance today, with the Pacific remaining stable while other regions eased slightly. In the Continent and Mediterranean, rates saw little change, although the market remained soft and below earlier levels. In the South Atlantic, fundamentals weakened considerably, causing rates to decline rapidly. The US Gulf stayed quiet due to a lack of fresh demand, keeping rates broadly unchanged. Activity across Asia was relatively muted, though sentiment remained steady despite limited fixing. The Eva Bright (40,577 2023) open Incheon fixed at $18,500 for a trip to Continent by Panocean, but further details were not disclosed. Overall, reflecting the mixed regional trend, the 7TC index slipped by $35 to finish at $15,304.

Market Fundamentals
Tata Steel India Drives Record FY2026 Performance Amid Strong Domestic Demand

Tata Steel delivered a record performance in FY2026 (y/e 31 Mar 2026), with consolidated crude steel production rising 2.5% year-on-year to 31.67 Mt and total sales reaching 31.97 Mt (+6% y-o-y). Growth was led by record high operations in India, where production climbed 8% to 23.43 Mt and domestic sales surged 12% to 22.53 Mt, with construction & infrastructure accounting for the highest demand share (5.2 Mt), followed by auto & ancillary (5.1 Mt), and retail (3.5 Mt) of the total sales.

The company remains optimistic on India’s steel consumption outlook, forecasting long-term consumption growth of 8-10% annually, above GDP growth of 6-7%. Meanwhile, European operations continue to face regulatory pressures and weak demand conditions, with Tata Steel Netherlands producing 1.63 Mt (-6.9%) of liquid steel during the year, with UK deliveries also down 17.5% year-on-year to 0.52 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was supported today, despite a weaker physical market with the index losing another $574. The May was paid to a high of 42000 in huge volume early on, before falling back down to 41250. Jun remained strong with pays up to 38750 and similarly the July contract, with 35000 paid. The Jun v Jul spread widens and strengthened up to 3500. Q3 volumes were good also with a range of 33100-33600 and the Q4 31900-32300. BALLASTER LISTS REMAIN MANAGEABLE, AND THERE IS NO REAL PRESSURE ON OWNERS TO CHASE LOWER LEVELS FOR NOW. OUTLOOK: WHILE THE MARKET HAS LOST SOME OF THE MOMENTUM SEEN LAST WEEK, OVERALL LEVELS REMAIN HEALTHY AND THE ATLANTIC CONTINUES TO TRADE ON A FIRM BASE. ACTIVITY HAS BEEN SLOWER THAN EXPECTED EARLY WEEK, BUT WITH TONNAGE STILL RELATIVELY TIGHT IN KEY AREAS, A PICKUP IN DEMAND THROUGH THE SECOND HALF OF THE WEEK COULD QUICKLY REBALANCE SENTIMENT. PAC SHORT: FOLLOWING THE POSITIVE SURGE IN RATES LAST WEEK, THE PACIFIC MARKET OPENED ON AN EXPECTEDLY QUIETER NOTE. DESPITE A SLOWDOWN IN FIXING ACTIVITY, DEMAND REMAINS RELATIVELY HEALTHY, PARTICULARLY FOR COAL EX INDO AND E.AUS INTO S.CHINA, WITH FURTHER SUPPORT COMING FROM KOREAN AND JAPANESE TENDERS. THERE HAS ALSO BEEN STEADY ENQUIRY FOR MINERALS, ALUMINA AND GRAIN CARGOES EX W.AUS. HOWEVER, IT APPEARS WE FOUND A CEILING LAST WEEK WITH NEGATIVE SENTIMENT ACROSS THE BASIN BEGINNING TO WEIGH ON THE MARKET. AUSTRALIA CONTINUES TO SEE THE STRONGEST DEMAND, ALTHOUGH TRADING IS SUBDUED. THERE WERE RUMOURS TUESDAY EVENING THAT ONE CHINESE OPERATOR WAS OFFERING USD 22.5K BKI CJK FOR AUS/S.CHINA ROUNDS FOR INDEX DATES, COMPARED TO USD 25K BEING OFFERED AT THE CLOSE OF LAST WEEK, DEMONSTRATING THE LACK OF SUPPORT FOR OWNERS ON THIS ROUTE. SPREADS FOR AUS RV ARE NOW AROUND USD

INDEX SEEN ON BOTH MONDAY AND TUESDAY, USD 23,920 (-174) AND USD 23,413 (-507) RESPECTIVELY, WE EXPECT FURTHER DOWNWARD PRESSURE ON PHYSICAL RATES HERE. ON MONDAY ONE KAMSARMAX EX N.CHINA WAS REPORTED FIXED FOR NOPAC GRAINS AT LOW USD 23K BKI CJK. BID/OFFER SPREADS FOR NOPAC GRAINS ARE NOW AROUND USD 21K VS USD 23K BKI CJK. FIXING LEVELS IN THE INDO MARKET HAVE TAKEN A BIG HIT. ALTHOUGH THERE HAS BEEN SOME FRESH DEMAND FOR END MAY-EARLY JUNE, THE SOUTH REMAINS OVERSUPPLIED FOR THESE DATES WHICH WILL LIKELY CONTINUE TO PUT PRESSURE RATES. AN LME EX S.CHINA WAS REPORTED FIXED ON TUESDAY AT LOW USD 21K BKI HONG KONG. OVERALL, WHILE THE MARKET BALANCE DOES NOT APPEAR MATERIALLY WEAK GIVEN THE CURRENT DEMAND PROFILE, INCREASINGLY NEGATIVE SENTIMENT AND A LACK OF FIXING MOMENTUM ARE LIKELY TO CONTINUE WEIGHING GRADUALLY ON RATES IN THE NEAR TERM. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场整体走弱，BDI下跌38点至3054，各船型指数普遍回落。Cape市场太平洋区域情绪改善但大西洋偏软，C5微涨0.15至14.94，BCI 5TC下跌574至44888；Panamax和Supramax均录得指数下跌，FFA曲线近月显著贴水，Supramax表现相对抗跌，仅下跌27点。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize太平洋基本面转暖，三大矿商在C5活跃度提升，费率从低位逐步抬升；大西洋C3受制于需求低迷，费率承压下行。Panamax大西洋前运和东海岸南美持续走弱，亚洲北太平洋供给过剩局面未改。Supramax大西洋美湾维持需求但预期差距扩大，亚洲开端缓慢供给压力显现。Handysize太平洋持稳，其他区域小幅走软。整体运力供给宽松而需求支撑不足，市场情绪偏空。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: FFA市场看空情绪明显：Cape5TC近月全线贴水，May26合约下跌500至41500下方；Panamax5TC各期限全面下跌，Jun26暴跌663点至20538。实物市场C5触底反弹但动力有限，C3持续阴跌。Panamax供给压力突出，印尼及北太平洋航线费率大幅回落。Supramax基本面偏中性，费率区间整理。Handysize稳中偏弱，无明显方向。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C5太平洋区域费率反弹持续性及三大矿商后续发货节奏。Panamax关注近月合约贴水修复机会及亚洲煤炭货盘释放情况。Supramax美湾需求支撑尚存但费率上行空间有限。FFA曲线近远月价差交易机会需关注。
